subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should chat.send keep immediate started ACK semantics for Codex sessions, or should oversized/unrunnable native-thread preflight be allowed to delay or fail the ACK before accepting the user message?
rationale: The current public contract intentionally ACKs before dispatch, while the reported failure needs a policy choice between preserving that contract with stronger async watchdogs or changing acceptance semantics for Codex liveness failures.

options.title: Keep open for liveness contract
options.body: Require a current-main live or fixture replay, then implement either forced rotation or visible failure while preserving the chosen chat.send contract.

options.title: Fail fast before ACK
options.body: Allow Codex native-thread preflight to block or reject chat.send started when no run can safely begin, trading compatibility risk for stronger user-visible correctness.

options.title: Preserve ACK and add watchdogs
options.body: Keep immediate ACKs but add auditable dispatch/run-start watchdogs and health recovery that persist the user turn and surface failure if Codex never starts.

recommendation.title: Keep open for liveness contract
recommendation.body: Require a current-main live or fixture replay, then implement either forced rotation or visible failure while preserving the chosen chat.send contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current native Codex overflow rotation mitigation most directly tied to the reported oversized-thread surface.
